title: #71 Lodewijk Petram: The World's First Stock Exchange

reader_summary.headline: Hello everyone and welcome to investing by the books, a podcast by Radei.
reader_summary.overview: Hello everyone and welcome to investing by the books, a podcast by Radei. I'm your host, Edipalmian and with me in the studio is my friend and colleague Niklas Savos. In this episode, we are delighted to have Ludovic Petram on the show.

key_points.text: Ludovic is an economist and historian working as a senior researcher with the Huygens Institute in Amsterdam, Netherlands.
key_points.evidence_quote: Ludovic is an economist and historian working as a senior researcher with the Huygens Institute in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

key_points.text: So Niklas, which book will we speak about?
key_points.evidence_quote: So Niklas, which book will we speak about?

key_points.text: So today we will speak about Ludovic's book, The World's First Stock Exchange.
key_points.evidence_quote: So today we will speak about Ludovic's book, The World's First Stock Exchange, where we get to learn about the listing and trading of the Dutch East India Company during the 17th century.

key_points.text: It's a really fascinating story which provides investors with a lot of perspective which is often the case with historical books.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's a really fascinating story which provides investors with a lot of perspective which is often the case with historical books, shares have been bought and sold for over 400 years and while a lot has changed over time, the human psyche remains the same.
